The process of electrolysis, which is an essential method for the production of hydrogen, involves several variables that can be altered, such as the viscosity of the current, the temperature, and the electrolyte attention. When it comes to successfully exploring the complicated, multidimensional parameter space, traditional optimization approaches typically fail to meet expectations. In this study, we make use of sophisticated machine-learning techniques to model and optimize these parameters. Our objective is to maximize the amount of hydrogen produced while simultaneously decreasing the amount of energy consumed and the costs associated with its operation. Through a series of trials and simulations, we demonstrate how machine literacy models, including retrogression and bracket algorithms, can prognosticate optimal settings and expose perceptivity into the electrolysis process. Our findings demonstrate considerable improvements in the efficiency of hydrogen products, demonstrating the possibility of incorporating machine literacy into electrochemical processes in the future.

articleTitle: The Identification of Anomalies in Surveillance Video using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Surveillance systems in the modern era heavily depend on computer vision for detecting anomalies in security footage. Real-time video feeds may be monitored and evaluated with the use of this feature, which includes object identification, motion tracking, and face detection. The system is able to distinguish between typical and suspicious actions thanks to automated anomaly detection and labeling. The technology delivers real-time warnings and messages when abnormalities are found, allowing security professionals and administrators to react quickly. In addition, the system keeps a log of past abnormalities, making it easier to conduct post-event research and gather evidence for investigations. One-Class SVM is used for supervised anomaly detection based on normal class boundaries, while Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are used for unsupervised anomaly detection through generated sequences, and 3D Convolutional Networks are used for spatial-temporal analysis to improve the surveillance system's anomaly detection capabilities.By integrating these computer vision methods and technologies, security systems may better protect vital regions and take a preventative approach to detecting anomalies, making the world a safer and more secure place for everyone.

articleTitle: Applying Hybrid Machine Learning Algorithm to Measure Total Lung Capacity from Spirometric Values
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The accurate diagnosis of restrictive ventilatory impairment requires the measurement of Total Lung Capacity (TLC), a process that typically involves complex and resource-intensive techniques like plethysmography or gas dilution. However, these advanced methods are often unavailable in routine clinical settings, creating a need for alternative approaches that leverage more accessible tools, such as spirometry. This study proposes a machine learning- based system that estimates TLC directly from spirometry data using advanced tree-based models, aiming to streamline the diagnostic pathway for restrictive lung diseases. By accurately predicting TLC from standard spirometric metrics, this approach can identify patients who would most benefit from further pulmonary function testing (PFT), reducing the need for additional, costly testing procedures. Comparative analyses were conducted between the machine learning model and Conventional Spirometry-based restriction predictionpatterns, showing improved accuracy and reliability in identifying restrictive impairments. The proposed system demonstrates significant potential as a decision- support tool, enhancing clinical workflows by prioritizing patients for full PFTs and improving access to timely and accurate diagnosis of restrictive ventilatory impairments.

articleTitle: A Framework of Intensive Dashboard to Highlight the Financial Insight Using PowerBI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The project is about the development of a comprehensive personal finance dashboard using Power BI. The dashboard is designed to empower users and administrators with tools to effectively manage and compare financial data. By integrating data transformation techniques and role-based access control, the dashboard offers a holistic view of income, expenses, and savings. It provides actionable insights through various visualizations, helping users achieve financial freedom. Key features include an intuitive interface for tracking financial metrics, detailed visualizations like bar graphs and line plots, and the ability to compare data over different periods. The project focuses on data integration, transformation, and security, ensuring personalized views and data privacy through Row-Level Security (RLS). The dashboard ultimately aims to assist users in setting realistic financial goals and making informed decisions.

articleTitle: An Upscaled Framework for Emotional Reponse System: A Support Solution from AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Virtual assistants have become essential in simplifying tasks in our busy lives. These advancements in artificial intelligence could become even more impactful by incorporating voice emotion recognition, enabling more natural, personalized interactions without constant typing. In this research, we introduce KANMANI, a model built on Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and AI to enhance virtual assistance by facilitating voice and video interactions with emotion and speech recognition. This responsive design is invaluable for users seeking connection even when alone. KANMANI's core objective is to “Empower minds and ignite possibilities by unlocking the future through personalized technology.” Structurally, KANMANI integrates three key components, each tailored for an intuitive user experience. The first, the Voice Assistant, utilizes AI and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to interpret spoken commands, creating seamless interaction. The second, Emotion Detection, identifies user emotions via speech and facial expressions, responding appropriately-such as with an encouraging quote. The final component, the Virtual Assistant, enables video-based interaction with real-time emotion detection, delivering responses that reflect empathy and awareness. Together, these features make KANMANI a customized virtual companion that supports and adapts to the user's world, offering practical assistance and emotional connection.

articleTitle: Utilising Convolutional Neural Networks for the Automated Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy has emerged as one of the leading causes of eye diseases among people suffering from long-term diabetes. Indeed, it raises the risk of being blinded without proper detection and treatment. Conventional detection of retinal fundus images by an ophthalmologist is time-consuming and prone to mistakes owing to human intervention. This is particularly a cause for alarm in the wake of the growing incidence of diabetes globally. The need for automated, accurate detection systems for early diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy has never been more relevant. In this work, we develop a deep learning model based on CNN for classifying four stages of diabetic retinopathy, from no DR to proliferative DR. We tested the model in a public dataset to extract features from retinal images and to screen for abnormalities automatically. Our CNN model achieved 98.5% classification and detection accuracy, thus indicating the ability to make a real difference in the early detection and treatment plan, thereby preserving the vision of many diabetic patients. Practical value The present research is very relevant to clinical practice and, therefore, practically useful because of its relevance to healthcare technology. Using accuracy and loss function metrics, the proposed model performs well compared to the latest techniques in DR detection. An approach based on CNNs is expected to ease much of the workload that healthcare professionals bear in diagnosis and improve the precision, potentially resulting in a very high cutback in vision loss in diabetic patients with better patient outcomes. Our study has highlighted the practical utility of the CNN model, which has improved patient outcomes. DR is a serious condition affecting the eyes, which, in case of untimely detection and untreated in diabetic patients, can cause loss of vision. For centuries, the conventional diagnosis for this disease has been through the manual inspection of retinal fundus images taken through a camera by an ophthalmologist. It is the slowest and most error-prone because it relies on human integrity. The rising worldwide current cases of diabetes pose an imperative for the development of more automation and specificity of the detection instruments towards early diagnosis of DR, an aim of this study.

Author Keywords: Early diagnosis and Vision loss prevention

articleTitle: Smart Business with Intelligent Business Cards (SBIBC)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The research emphasizes the creation of a powerful and efficient system for the automaticextraction of contact information from physical calling cards through computer vision and information extraction techniques. This is achieved by integrating Tesseract Optical Character Recognition (OCR) with the YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm, which acts as a dynamic combination for text and relevant elements identification and digitization from calling cards. The developed system uses client-server architecture to enable communication and data processing seamlessly. The server handles computationally intensive tasks such as object detection, OCR processing, and data validation while the client side has an interactive user interface that enables easy uploading of images and retrieval of structured contact information. The optimizations include this: YOLO is customized for detecting particular card elements (name, phone number, email) and enhancing the capabilities of Tesseract OCR to improve effectiveness for text extraction from varied card formats or fonts in the system. It is designed to be scalable and efficient, processing large datasets without affecting accuracy. This approach not only eases the digitization of calling card details into databases but also goes a long way in contributing to the domains of computer vision, object detection, and mechanized information extraction. It extends the scope to broad applications in automated data entry, customer relationship management (CRM), and digital archival. It takes forward for AI-driven sustaining technologies the integration of these techniques into practical solutions by overcoming the challenges of data extraction from real-world images.

articleTitle: Ransomware Detection Using Quantum Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Ransomware is a malicious software (malware) that encodes the files on a victim’s computer or network, which makes them inaccessible. Once the files are encoded, the intruder typically claims a ransom, often in cryptocurrency, in return for the decoding key that gives access to the files. Preventing ransomware attacks usually involves a combination of security protocols, including regular data backups, user education, and the use of antivirus software. An innovative approach is proposed for the ransomware detection using Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs), harnessing the guidelines of quantum computing to amplify detection precision and optimization of the network. This technique involves training a QNN on labeled datasets of ransomware and benign software, focusing on detecting anomalies in file behavior, encryption patterns, and system interactions. Random undersampling is a mechanism designed to address class imbalance in datasets, particularly in organizing tasks. It consists of reducing The total count in the majority category to equalize the class distribution. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance in early-stage ransomware detection with improved false-positive rates and reduced computational overhead. Further research will focus on optimizing the QNN architecture and researching hybrid models that harmonize conventional and quantum techniques. The goal is to amplify the scalability and productivity of ransomware detection structures in dynamic threat landscapes.

articleTitle: Enhanced Energy-Efficient Routing in WSNs: A Multipath Approach Using Binary Gray Wolf Optimization and Sugeno Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are pivotal in enabling real-time Internet of Things (IoT) applications through sensor nodes that communicate both with each other and their environment. Despite their potential, WSNs face significant challenges due to limited energy resources, which are crucial for sustaining long-term operations. One of the most pressing issues is unbalanced energy utilization during data packet routing, which can lead to premature network failure. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing an Enhanced Zone Stable Election Multipath Routing Protocol that leverages Binary Gray Wolf Optimization (BGWO) and Sugeno Fuzzy Logic. The proposed protocol aims to enhance energy efficiency, load balancing, and network scalability through an optimized clustering and routing approach. By employing multipath routing, the protocol creates multiple paths between source and destination, thereby improving data delivery probability and network resilience. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods, such as LEACH and DFLC, in terms of packet delivery ratio, energy consumption and network life time. The findings suggest that the proposed solution significantly extends network lifetime and improves overall performance, offering a robust alternative to conventional WSN routing strategies.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Digital Forensic Data for Unbreakable Trust and Security
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: This can be one of the most magnificent advantages realized from applying blockchain technology in a forensic investigation context, namely, a transformative approach to address challenges embedded within legal and criminal justice systems. For example, smart contracts, being self-executing agreements with the automated inclusion of predefined rules, may even automate and secure the process of tracking evidence, managing chain of custody, and access control. This smart contract will ensure that forensic operations are transparent and of sound integrity. Every transaction and action performed on the blockchain is recorded there, instantaneously bringing down tampering to the lowest possibility and any chance for human mistakes. Regarding decentralized nature and cryptography-based security combined with immutability, blockchain is a technology known to have safeguards over sensitive data. Once recorded on the blockchain, the information thereupon becomes completely un-changeable, assuring the reliability and authenticity of evidence. This will be especially important in the management of an unforgeable chain of custody and in ensuring that forensic evidence remains unchanged and can be relied on with integrity throughout the court process.[6] Critical data can then be maintained tamper-proof for management and storage by developing Ethereum-based smart contracts on Remix IDE using Solidity.[15]Each transaction will be time-stamped and safely logged on the Ethereum blockchain, thus developing an unchallenged ledger that makes any investigation that much more trustworthy. In a nutshell, the application of blockchain in forensic activities builds greater control and efficiencies, reduces possible errors and conflicts, and provides transparency, integrity, and an unchangeable, permanent record for forensic processes. The invention thereby significantly upgrades the general integrity and confidence in legal and criminal justice inquiries.

articleTitle: Multimodal Deep Learning for Precise Lung Pathology Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a serious airborne infectious disease with a high fatality rate, primarily affecting the lungs. Early detection is vital for effective treatment, yet the current healthcare landscape suffers from a significant shortage of medical professionals and screening facilities, which hinders timely diagnosis. The lung cancer pandemic has further exacerbated these challenges, straining healthcare systems and complicating diagnostic procedures for respiratory diseases. Existing diagnostic systems predominantly rely on the ResNet algorithm to predict TB. However, these systems often fall short when it comes to accurately diagnosing COVID- 19, leading to reduced prediction accuracy and missed opportunities for early intervention. In light of these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid approach that combines Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to facilitate the simultaneous prediction of both TB and LUNG CANCER. The integration of RNNs allows for effective temporal analysis of sequential data, while CNNs excel in extracting spatial features from medical imaging, such as X-rays or CT scans. This synergistic model is designed to improve the predictive accuracy for both diseases by leveraging the strengths of each architecture. By enhancing feature extraction and analysis capabilities, this innovative approach aims to address the pressing need for reliable diagnostic tools in the face of inadequate healthcare resources. Ultimately, the future system has the efficiency to enable earlier diagnoses and the treatment outcomes, and contribute to better public health management during dual outbreaks of TB and lung cancer.

articleTitle: Design a 6 GHz MODEM for Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANET's)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: The Design of 6 GHz Modem for Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs), utilizing a Cyclonic II FPGA, a 6 GHz Low Noise Broadband Signal Amplifier (LNA), and an infrared IC encoder/decoder. The modem operates in the 6 GHz frequency band to provide high-speed, low-latency communication crucial for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) interactions, enhancing traffic safety and autonomous driving. The modem achieves a minimum throughput of 100 Mbps, with latency below 10 ms, ensuring real-time data exchange. The system maintains a packet loss rate below 0.01%, supported by a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 20 dB and a bit error rate (BER) lower than 10- 5. It covers a minimum area of 12 meters, making it suitable for dynamic vehicular environments. Operating with a channel bandwidth of 100 MHz, the modem integrates adaptive modulation and interference mitigation techniques for reliable communication in varying conditions. Simulation results confirm its robustness, paving the way for future smart transportation systems in the 6 GHz spectrum.

articleTitle: Assessing Landslide Susceptibility in Active Tectonic Zones using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Assessing landslide susceptibility is vital in mitigating natural disasters, particularly in zones with active tectonics. This paper will discuss a novel approach based on a CNN architecture in a U -Net designed to assess landslide susceptibility in these zones of active tectonism. The model thus takes advantage of spatial data sources from remote sensing and GIS and multi-coupled geospatial factors such as slope, elevation, rainfall, and tectonic activity in a multivariate framework for predicting landslide-prone areas. The U-Net CNN architecture is used as it captures the local and global spatial patterns and results in very precise susceptibility maps. The selected historical data about landslides was then fed into the trained and validated model to predict potential landslide occurrence zones, indicating high accuracy in susceptibility mapping. The CNN-based U-Net approach suggests a higher order of precision and spatial resolution than the conventional machine learning approach. This work portrays the capabilities of deep learning approaches in developing landslide risk assessment with much-improved precision. It thus offers an essential tool for disaster risk management along with urban planning for tectonically active regions.

articleTitle: Evaluating Data and Power Transmission Efficiency Through Free Space Optics Under Atmospheric Turbulence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: In today's world, wireless data and power transmission systems are challenged with significant obstacles, particularly those arising from atmospheric turbulence and environmental conditions. The increasing complexity of network infrastructures, coupled with challenges posed by adverse weather, further complicates the reliability and efficiency of these systems. To address these issues, we propose a technique using Free Space Optics (FSO) to enable real-time data and power transmission wirelessly. FSO offers advantages over traditional RF-based wireless communication, such as lower cost, higher speeds, increased data rates, and broader bandwidth. Unlike RF, which relies on licensed bands, FSO operates on an unlicensed spectrum, providing a promising alternative. However, atmospheric conditions pose difficulties for FSO-based communication. This paper evaluates the performance of the proposed system under different weather conditions, including clear skies, haze, heavy rain, and various levels of fog. The system's performance is analyzed in terms of visibility range, quality factor, bit error rate (BER), and eye diagrams across varying atmospheric scenarios.

articleTitle: Integrating Lightweight Algorithms with Blockchain for Secure and Efficient Authentication in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Vehicular Ad Hoc Networks (VANETs) play a pivotal role in enabling secure communication for intelligent transportation systems. However, existing authentication mechanisms often face challenges such as high computational overhead, scalability issues, and latency, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates lightweight algorithms with Blockchain technology to achieve secure and efficient authentication in VANETs. The proposed approach leverages Blockchain's decentralized trust management and tamper-proof ledger with the computational efficiency of lightweight algorithms like TESLA. This integration enables real-time authentication while ensuring data integrity, privacy, and scalability. The framework is designed to minimize latency and communication overhead, making it suitable for high-density urban environments. A detailed performance evaluation demonstrates the efficacy of the proposed method, highlighting significant improvements in scalability, security, and resource efficiency. This study provides a promising direction for addressing the diverse requirements of VANET applications while maintaining robust security standards.

articleTitle: Improving the Accuracy of Sarcasm Detection in Text Data Using a Smooth Support Vector Classification Model with Word-Emoji Embedding for News and Indian Indigenous Languages
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: By creating a Smooth Support Vector Classification (SSVC) model linked with word-emoji embedded data that is especially suited for newspapers and native Indian languages, the study aims to improve sarcasm detection in textual information. Because sarcasm is context-dependent and subtle, it poses a considerable barrier to processing natural speech, especially in multilingual situations. Word-emoji embedding is used by the proposed SSVC model to capture nuanced textual clues, emotions, and moods frequently overlooked by existing methods. The more emotional context that emojis offer to language data, the more precisely the algorithm can identify sarcasm. The paper tackles the complexity of multilingual sarcasm, concentrating on Indian indigenous languages, which are frequently underrepresented in NLP studies and lack adequate annotated information. The model performs better in classification than typical SVM models, as evidenced by extensive trials on real-world datasets of news items and social media chats. With applications in improving the interaction between humans and computers controlling online material, the study advances sentiment analysis, especially in various language circumstances.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Isolated DC-DC Converter with MultiResonant Circuit for Wide Output EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: A new method for creating an isolated DC-DC converter system using a Multi-Resonant Circuit (MRC) for effective electric vehicle (EV) charging is presented. The research investigates how power electronics and transformer technology can be used to overcome the problem of a broad output voltage range in EV charging applications. The importance of isolated converters in EV power systems is explained through a thorough literature study, along with developments in MRC technology. The methodology emphasizes the importance of transformers in attaining galvanic isolation while providing specifics on the design and implementation process. The efficacy of the suggested system in converting DC voltage levels while retaining high efficiency is shown by simulation results. Findings and analysis contrast the suggested system with current approaches, emphasizing useful implications and performance measures. The study's conclusions include suggestions for more research projects as well as an analysis of the suggested system's contributions to the field of power electronics in EV charging.

articleTitle: Leveraging Deep Sequential Convolutional Neural Networks in Digital Transformation for Sustainable E-Waste Management in the New Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on System, Computation, Automation and Networking (ICSCAN)
abstract: Rapid technical breakthroughs in the current digital age have contributed to the creation of electronic waste (e-waste) poses serious threats to health and the environment. This research examines the use of Deep Sequential Convolutional Neural Networks (DSCNNs) to leverage the Internet of Things (IoT) for sustainable management of electronic waste. The global e-waste dilemma is introduced with a focus on the need for innovative solutions to mitigate its impact. Existing challenges include the increasing number of discarded electronic devices, ineffective e-waste sorting, and limited recycling options. DSCNN models for their strong visual recognition capabilities, offer viable solutions by automating e-waste classification and recycling. This research explores various DSCNN architectures and their applications in e-waste processing devices to enable faster and more accurate recognition of recyclable materials. The primary goal is to develop an efficient DSCNN-based framework to enhance recycling efficiency, reduce landfill inputs, and promote sustainable practices. Preliminary findings suggest that DSCNN models significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of e-waste sorting, paving the way for scalable and cost-effective e-waste management platforms. By addressing key environmental issues, this research advocates for the integration of AI technology into waste management processes.
